reason: This passage from Nehemiah 2 depicts Nehemiah securing authorization from King Artaxerxes to rebuild Jerusalem's walls and subsequently mobilizing the people for this work. While Nehemiah's leadership does result in material benefits to the people (restoration of their city), the text does not present 'a functioning government to the benefit of the people' as its model of good leadership. Instead, the passage emphasizes: (1) divine providence—'God's hand was good upon me'; (2) personal religious devotion and prayer as the foundation of leadership; and (3) the religious/spiritual restoration of God's people and God's city as the ultimate goal. The governmental elements (the king's authorization, organizational structure) are instrumental means to achieve this religious end, not the model of good leadership itself. The text frames leadership through a theological lens of God's guidance and restoration, not through political governance as a primary value.
